{"answer": "Note: the schema offers no enumerated options; answer is given in the four required parts, with the swap-condition sentence at the end.

1. WHAT IS SOLD
F1 FACT [10-Q, Revenue by Technology]: "DRAM | $7,071 | $4,692 | $19,594 | $12,277" and "NAND | 2,155 | 2,065 | 6,251 | 4,862" (Q3 FY25 / Q3 FY24 / YTD).
F2 FACT [Certain Concentrations]: nine-month revenue mix "Data center and networking 55%", "Mobile 15%", "PC, graphics, and other 15%", intelligent edge "15%"; "Revenue from one customer was 16%".
F3 FACT [Risk Factors]: "We face intense competition... from a number of companies, including Kioxia... Samsung... SK hynix... Sandisk... YMTC... and CXMT"; "Our competitors may use aggressive pricing to obtain market share."
I1 INFERENCE (F1–F3): the buyer is choosing mainly on price/performance-per-bit and qualification among a handful of suppliers of substitutable bits, concentrated in data-center accounts.

2. SALE-TO-CASH
F4 FACT [Revenue note]: "Revenue is primarily recognized at a point in time when control of the promised goods is transferred... Substantially all contracts with our customers are short-term in duration at fixed, negotiated prices with payment generally due shortly after delivery."
F5 FACT [Receivables]: "Trade receivables | $5,492 | $5,419".
F6 FACT [Revenue note]: customer prepayments and other contract liabilities "were $146 million and $907 million"; "$777 million from shipments against customer prepayments"; "other current liabilities included $807 million... for estimates of consideration payable to customers including estimates for pricing adjustments and returns".
I2 INFERENCE (F4–F6): cash follows shipment by roughly one payment cycle; prepayments, which funded shipments earlier, have largely been consumed, and $807M of accrued price adjustments sits between billed and final price.

3. COST STRUCTURE
F7 FACT [Risk Factors]: "A significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed and do not vary proportionally with changes in production output."
F8 FACT [Cash flows, 9M]: "Depreciation expense and amortization of intangible assets | 6,203" against "Cost of goods sold | 16,244".
F9 FACT [Liquidity]: "capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion."
F10 FACT [Risk Factors]: "HBM requires a higher number of wafers to produce the same number of bits as conventional DRAM in the same technology node"; costs vary with "fabrication facility underutilization, lower wafer output"; "a significant portion of our manufacturing costs are denominated in some of the foreign currencies".
I3 INFERENCE (F7–F10): the ratio moves with utilization, node transition and HBM mix; depreciation from the ~$14bn capex programme enters COGS regardless of bits sold.

4. RANKED PROFIT DRIVERS
F11 FACT [MD&A]: gross margin "38% for the third quarter of 2025 from 27% for the third quarter of 2024... primarily due to increases in average selling prices for DRAM products, manufacturing cost reductions, and an increased mix in sales of high-margin cloud products, particularly HBM."
F12 FACT [Risk Factors]: "annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range."
F13 FACT [Segment]: "CNBU | $2,182 | 43%" vs "SBU | (9) | (1)%" (Q3 FY25 operating income and margin).
(a) DRAM ASP — F11/F12: named first in every margin bridge, with the widest disclosed range. (b) Mix toward HBM/cloud DRAM — F11/F13: the segment carrying HBM earned 43% operating margin while the NAND-centric segment was at break-even. (c) Per-bit cost/utilization — F7/F11: cited as a contributor, but always second to price in the MD&A bridges.

SWAP CONDITION: I would move mix above ASP if Micron disclosed HBM revenue and HBM gross margin separately and they showed HBM profit rising in a quarter when DRAM ASPs fell.", "what_i_do_not_understand": "HBM unit economics. FACT [MD&A]: "CNBU revenue increased 11% primarily due to higher sales of HBM products, which increased nearly 50%" — the bundle gives HBM only as a growth rate inside CNBU, never HBM revenue, price, cost per bit or margin, and FACT [Segment note]: "Other indirect operating income and expenses are generally allocated to segments based on their respective percentage of cost of goods sold or forecasted wafer production", so CNBU's 43% margin is partly an allocation artefact. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE — needed: HBM revenue, HBM gross margin, and the fixed/variable split of COGS plus fab utilisation; why: the bundle contains only qualitative statements ("a significant portion of our manufacturing costs are fixed") and segment operating income built on a cost-of-goods-sold allocation key; would_change: if HBM margin were disclosed and materially above the 38% consolidated gross margin, the profit engine is a contracted, design-won product and my ranking flips toward mix; if HBM margin were near consolidated, the engine is commodity DRAM price and the ASP ranking stands. I also do not know what fraction of the $2,169m Q3 operating income depends on capacity that is not yet depreciating — construction in progress is "$4,937" and equipment not in service "$3.40 billion", and the bundle does not say when those enter cost."}
